subtopics.title: What Development Means — and What It Does Not

questions.question: Why is economic growth described as necessary but not sufficient for development?
options: Growth enlarges the economy's output, but development requires that the new wealth actually improves lives — health, education, services — and growth can pool in few hands instead
Growth and development are two words for the same thing
Development happens only when growth stops
Growth measures quality of life directly

questions.question: A miner earns a good salary but works in a dangerous shaft and breathes coal dust. The correct description is:
options: High quality of life, low standard of living
A reasonable standard of living but a poor quality of life, because quality of life includes health, safety and environment beyond income
Both high, since salary determines everything
Neither term applies to individuals

questions.question: South Korea, Brazil and Mexico — countries whose manufacturing surged within living memory — are labelled:
options: LEDCs
MEDCs
NICs — newly industrialised countries
First World countries

questions.question: The CAPS definition of development is best summarised as:
options: The growth of a country's total output
The process of building more factories
An increase in exports
The process of improving people's quality of life — wealth together with health, education, safety, freedom and dignity

subtopics.title: Measuring Development in Money: GDP, GNP and the Gini Coefficient

questions.question: A Toyota plant operating in Durban counts inside:
options: South Africa's GDP but Japan's GNP, because GDP counts production within borders while GNP counts production by a country's citizens and companies anywhere
South Africa's GNP but Japan's GDP
Both countries' GDP
Neither country's accounts

questions.question: Why is GDP per capita a fairer comparison tool than total GDP?
options: It removes inflation from the figures
Dividing by population gives output per person, so a small rich country is no longer out-ranked by a large poor one simply because of population size
It counts only exports
It includes the Gini coefficient automatically

questions.question: The Gini coefficient runs on a scale where:
options: 0 means one person earns everything and 1 means perfect equality
0 means no economy exists
0 means everyone earns the same and 1 means one person earns everything
100 is the maximum score

questions.question: South Africa's Gini coefficient of about 0,63 tells us:
options: The country is poorer than its neighbours
Average income is falling
GDP is inaccurate
Income is distributed extremely unequally — a respectable average income coexists with deep poverty, which per capita figures alone cannot show

subtopics.title: Beyond Money: HDI and the Social Indicators

questions.question: Infant mortality is called the most sensitive development indicator because:
options: Keeping babies alive demands everything working at once — maternal care, immunisation, sanitation and income — so the number reflects the whole system
Babies are counted more accurately than adults
It is the only indicator measured yearly
It depends on income alone

questions.question: The three dimensions combined in the Human Development Index are:
options: Exports, imports and savings
Health (life expectancy), education (years of schooling) and income (GNI per capita)
Population, area and resources
GDP, GNP and the Gini coefficient

questions.question: South Africa's HDI of about 0,71 trails its income ranking mainly because:
options: Schooling years are the lowest in Africa
The rand is weak
The health dimension — life expectancy in the mid-sixties — drags the combined score down despite relatively strong income and schooling
HDI ignores income entirely

questions.question: The HDI's designed advantage over GDP-based measures is that:
options: It is easier to calculate
It uses a larger scale
It changes more slowly
A country cannot buy a good score with money alone, so the index exposes the gap between wealth and wellbeing that GDP hides

questions.question: The Brandt line of 1980:
options: Split the world into a rich North and poor South, dipping to include Australia and New Zealand — a useful first sketch that has since blurred as countries like South Korea rose
Divided Africa from Asia
Marked the equator
Still describes the world with perfect accuracy

questions.question: Describing development as a continuum means:
options: Countries alternate between rich and poor each decade
Countries are strung along a line from lowest to highest development with every position filled, rather than clustering into two camps
Only two categories of country exist
Development cannot be measured

questions.question: Sandton and Diepsloot sharing one metro demonstrates that:
options: The Brandt line runs through Johannesburg
Urban areas are always developed
Development differences run within countries as sharply as between them, which is why the Gini coefficient matters
Averages describe cities accurately

questions.question: The balanced examination answer on South Africa's development status is:
options: A fully developed MEDC because of the JSE
An LEDC because of unemployment
Impossible to classify
A developing country — an NIC — with pockets of MEDC prosperity and pockets of LEDC deprivation, supported by evidence on income, HDI, unemployment and inequality

questions.question: In the two-streets picture, development is:
options: The work of moving the second street toward the first — medicine, taps, teachers and safety, not only money
Building a wall between the streets
Moving people from the second street to the first
Raising the first street's incomes further

questions.question: The man with a good salary living beside a burning mine dump shows:
options: That salaries determine quality of life
A standard of living without the matching quality of life, because quality of life includes health, safety and clean air
That mine dumps raise property values
Neither concept applies

questions.question: The factory that doubles output while every extra rand leaves town illustrates:
options: Development without growth
Neither growth nor development
Growth without development — the engine revving without the wheels turning
Sustainable development

questions.question: In the soccer scoreboard picture, dividing total goals by the number of teams stands for:
options: Calculating GDP per capita — output per person — so big populations stop distorting the comparison
Calculating the Gini coefficient
Converting GDP to GNP
Adjusting for inflation

questions.question: Goals scored inside your own stadium by anyone, versus goals scored by your registered players anywhere, stands for:
options: Exports versus imports
GDP — production within borders — versus GNP, production by a country's citizens and companies wherever they operate
Standard of living versus quality of life
HDI versus Gini

questions.question: One team winning 10-nil while forty-nine teams lose, yet the club average looking healthy, is the analogy for:
options: A high GDP growth rate
A trade surplus
South Africa's inequality — a decent average income beside a Gini coefficient of about 0,63
A strong currency

questions.question: The paired sentence worth carrying into the exam is:
options: The Gini measures the cake's size; GDP measures the slices
Both measures describe the cake's ingredients
Neither measure involves distribution
The average tells you the size of the cake per person; the Gini coefficient tells you how the cake is sliced

subtopics.title: The Report Card With Three Subjects

questions.question: The three subjects on the HDI report card are:
options: Health via life expectancy, education via schooling years, and income per person
Exports, currency strength and savings
Population, urbanisation and area
GDP, GNP and Gini

questions.question: Why can a country not 'cram one subject' to top the HDI class?
options: The subjects are marked by different agencies
The index deliberately averages three dimensions, so wealth cannot buy a top score while health or education lag — which is how it catches rich-but-unwell countries
The income subject is excluded for rich countries
Only education counts in the final mark

questions.question: A falling infant mortality rate signals genuine development because:
options: It raises GDP directly
Fewer children means faster growth
Keeping a baby alive needs clinics, vaccines, clean water and income all working at the same time, so the falling number means the whole system is improving
It only reflects hospital numbers

questions.question: On the ladder picture of world development, South Africa stands:
options: On the top rung with Norway
On the bottom rung with Niger
Outside the ladder entirely
Mid-ladder — a developing country with one foot on a high rung and one on a low one, defended with evidence
